memory_candidates.content: A task's declared file_scope entry of the literal string __WHOLE_TREE__ (used to describe a phase whose 'Files to modify' is 'the entire deployed tree, regenerated by deploy-headless.sh') is NOT treated as a wildcard by git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check -- it is a plain string compared for exact/ancestor match like any other entry. A tracked file deploy-headless.sh itself rewrites (e.g. .claude-extensions.json) is still dropped as out-of-scope unless it is ALSO separately listed in file_scope, and must be landed via the mechanical follow-up-commit trigger (a scoped git-commit-scoped.sh call for that one path) rather than assumed covered by the __WHOLE_TREE__ marker.

sapience_notes.subject: Fixture-based linked-repo verification: scratch repo plus stubbed GET, reusing a real test fixture's cid/key pair
sapience_notes.value: To verify a linked-repo code path's done-when criterion without a permanent, undeletable write to the hosted vault, build a standalone scratch git repo carrying a .sapience/project.json binding and copy the deployed scripts (postflight-sapience-notes.sh, sapience-remember.sh, deploy-root-guard.sh, lib/common.sh) into a mirrored .claude/scripts/ tree inside it, with a PATH-shadowing curl stub answering only the one GET endpoint the dry-run path reaches (GET /v1/people/projects). Reusing an existing test suite's proven cid/key fixture pair (mEdYrFW_qClSGDfx / oliver-ben) keeps the fixture realistic without inventing new values. This exercises the production script end-to-end (not just its own narrower unit-test suite) while guaranteeing zero network reach to the real vault.

sapience_notes.subject: __WHOLE_TREE__ in a declared file_scope is a literal string, not a wildcard, for git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check
sapience_notes.value: A plan phase declaring Files to modify as __WHOLE_TREE__ (deploy-headless.sh regenerates the entire deployed tree) does not make git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check admit every file that regeneration touches. .claude-extensions.json (a tracked file deploy-headless.sh rewrites) was dropped as out-of-scope on the phase commit despite __WHOLE_TREE__ being present in the task's declared file_scope, because the Containment predicate does exact/ancestor path matching against each file_scope string, never pattern expansion. The drop was recovered correctly via the designed mechanism: git-commit-phase.sh deposited the dropped path into .return-meta.json's proposed_file_scope, and a scoped git-commit-scoped.sh follow-up commit (never a second git-commit-phase.sh call, which would re-run the same check and drop it again) landed it.

sapience_notes.subject: orchestrator-postflight.sh documents 'implement does inline' for the update-task-status.sh postflight call
sapience_notes.value: orchestrator-postflight.sh's own Stage 7 comment states its update-task-status.sh postflight call applies to research and plan operations only, because 'implement does inline' -- the completing implementation agent itself calls update-task-status.sh postflight directly when all plan phases are done, rather than waiting for the orchestrator's own postflight stage to do it. The final 'task {N}: complete implementation' git commit (covering the resulting specs/TODO.md and specs/state.json changes) and the sapience_notes vault write (postflight-sapience-notes.sh, gated on postflight_rc==0) are deliberately left to the orchestrator's own orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh stage, which runs after the implementation dispatch returns and reads its .orchestrator-handoff.json/.return-meta.json.

sapience_notes.subject: Vendor ~/.sapience source has zero link-state awareness in its transcript-classification path, confirmed by direct grep
sapience_notes.value: The claim that source_skip()'s subagent/harness-started classification is independent of Sapience project-link state (no .sapience/project.json awareness) was corroborated by a direct grep for 'project' across the installed vendor ~/.sapience/*.py files, which returned zero hits in that classification context -- not merely re-asserted from this repository's own documentation. This is the kind of claim worth verifying against the actual vendor-owned artifact when one is reachable, rather than trusting a repo-side description of code outside the repo.

sapience_notes.subject: A ruling's 'check' can split into a mechanically-verifiable half and a structurally agent-exercise-limited half
sapience_notes.value: When a documented verification check names behavior behind an AskUserQuestion-gated interactive skill (e.g. a /sapience draft naming a pending suggestion), the check should be split explicitly: the data-plumbing half (does the upstream data source correctly carry the fixture value through, e.g. sapience-vault-read.sh passing a non-empty vault.suggestions entry to its output unmodified) is run live and confirmed; the draft-generation half is recorded as a stated verification limit identical in kind to any other AskUserQuestion-withheld-from-Agent-dispatch limitation, never silently treated as passed and never silently skipped.
